title: False Friends Ambush
intro: Embarazada isn’t embarrassed. Actualmente isn’t actually. The words that look Spanish and betray you every time — match each one to what it really means.

A2.right: ashamed or awkward (not pregnant — that's 'embarazada' in Spanish)
a place to borrow books (not a bookshop — that's 'librería' in Spanish)
a floor covering (not a folder — that's 'carpeta' in Spanish)
the way out (not success — 'éxito' in Spanish means success)
big in size (not long in time — 'largo' in Spanish means long)
to fake something (not to expect or intend — 'pretender' in Spanish)
in fact, really (not 'currently' — that's 'actualmente' in Spanish)
to become aware of something (not to carry out — 'realizar' in Spanish)

B1.right: to help (not to attend an event — 'asistir' in Spanish means to attend)
kind and understanding (not fun or likeable — 'simpático' in Spanish means friendly)
practical and wise (not sensitive or emotional — 'sensible' in Spanish means sensitive)
unable to empty your bowels (not having a cold — 'constipado' in Spanish means a cold)
a disagreement or quarrel (not a film's plot — 'argumento' in Spanish means plot)
your working life (not a degree course — 'carrera' in Spanish often means degree)
real, as opposed to imagined (not 'current' — 'actual' in Spanish means present-day)
in the end, finally (not 'possibly' — 'eventualmente' in Spanish means possibly)

B2.right: a mutual concession (not a prior engagement — 'compromiso' in Spanish often means commitment)
strong revulsion (not mild annoyance — 'disgusto' in Spanish can mean upset)
to abuse sexually — a serious word (not to bother — 'molestar' in Spanish is much milder)
a formal talk or class (not reading — 'lectura' in Spanish means reading)
cloth or textile (not a factory — 'fábrica' in Spanish means factory)
mentally healthy (not healthy in general — 'sano' in Spanish means healthy)
the act of deceiving or lying (not disappointment — 'decepción' in Spanish means disappointment)
having good schooling (not polite — 'educado' in Spanish means well-mannered)

C1.right: in the end, finally (not 'recently' — 'últimamente' in Spanish means lately)
a fixed expression (not language in general — 'idioma' in Spanish means language)
excellent, wonderful (not terrifying, despite the look of the word)
polite and kind (not funny — 'gracioso' in Spanish means funny)
a person injured or killed (not something informal — 'casual' in Spanish means by chance)
your handwritten name (not a firm or company — 'firma' in Spanish can mean company)
an expression of regret (not a defence — 'apología' in Spanish can mean a defence of something)
the appearance of your skin (not a complicated situation — unrelated sense in Spanish)
